title: Decentralize RBAC graph cache and enforce KMS consent retention policy
author: Evelyn Cho
release_notes: Decentralizes the RBAC decision graph cache to per-operator pods, introduces KMS consent retention enforcement and adds immutable audit stamp headers. No API surface changes. Backwards-compatible config flags provided.
description: Motivation: previously the RBAC v2 policy graph and KMS consent enforcement were centralized in the policy service which caused spikes under operator-heavy workloads and created a single point for policy cache stomping. This PR decentralizes the policy graph cache to operator-local stores while adding a retention-aware KMS consent checker and immutable audit stamp propagation. Goals: reduce policy lookup latency under high concurrency; make per-operator policy decisions resilient to control-plane noise; ensure KMS consent entries respect retention policies and are auditable. What this PR does: 1) adds a per-operator rbac-graph cache component that subscribes to policy delta webhook events; 2) implements a retention-aware KMS consent validator that queries consent TTL metadata and rejects or soft-fails requests based on tenant policy; 3) augments outgoing audit headers with an immutable-audit-stamp (signed with service key) and a consent-hash to aid downstream deduplication; 4) introduces feature flags: rbacv2.decentralized_cache (opt-in), kms.consent_retention_enforce (default off for staged rollout); 5) provides migration shim that keeps centralized fallback for 30 days after rollout; 6) adds unit and integration tests plus a small perf microbenchmark harness. Backwards compatibility: control plane can still serve decisions; the decentralization is opt-in per-cluster via the feature flag. Deployment notes: staged rollout recommended per-region; operators must have access to the policy delta webhook and a local short-lived signing key stored in the existing operator KMS wrapper. See Linear ENG-1974 for timing and rollout plan. Checklist: - [x] implement decentralized cache and delta subscriber - [x] implement KMS consent retention checker - [x] wire immutable audit stamp header - [x] add feature flags and migration shim - [x] unit + integration tests - [x] performance microbench and dashboard update - [x] docs and runbook updates (docs/ops/rbacv2-decentralized.md) Links: design doc https://go.redwood/design/rbac-decentralized, runbook https://go.redwood/runbooks/rbac-decentralize, Linear ENG-1974.
commits_summary: 3 commits: initial decentralized cache skeleton; KMS consent retention validator + tests; audit header signing, tests, and docs. Each commit small and focused; signatures verified. Commit SHAs: a1b2c3d, d4e5f6a, f7e8d9c (squashed on merge).
diff_highlights: Added decen_cache.go: ~350 LOC implementing delta-apply and LRU eviction; validator.go: retention enforcement with soft-fail path; audit_stamp.go: signing helper using operator KMS wrapper; small wiring changes to operator bootstrap. No large protocol changes.
review_conversation: Sana: requested stronger metrics around cache misses and delta delivery latencies; noted potential build-up of stale policies during network partition. Evelyn: added metrics rbac.cache.misses and rbac.delta.latency and a periodic reconciliation routine; updated tests to simulate partition. Liam: asked about key rotation and immutable stamp revocation; Evelyn: clarified that stamps are short-lived (5m) and operator KMS wrapper rotates signing tokens as part of operator boot process; added docs. Marco: suggested a migration fence for 2 weeks before turning enforcement on; feature flags and migration shim added. Final approval given by Sana and Marco. CI green after two re-runs (flaky integration test fixed).
ci_checks: CI summary: lint passed; unit tests passed; integration suite initially failed on delta-delivery timeout (flaky), re-run passed; perf benchmark ran in CI smoke mode and showed 8-12% p50 improvement on policy lookup for multi-operator scenario. All checks passed before merge.
merge_outcome: merged on 2026-02-20 via squash merge by Evelyn Cho; merge commit includes summarized changelog and notes for operators. Post-merge: feature flag rollout started in us-west-2 as canary; telemetry dashboard updated.
operational_impact: Operators must ensure webhook connectivity and grant operator service the policy.subscribe permission; minor memory increase per operator for local cache (~40-80MB depending on policy set size). KMS usage will have additional metadata reads; observed CI microbench indicates CPU usage stable. No immediate customer-facing changes. Runbook and rollout steps included in docs/ops/rbacv2-decentralized.md.
follow_up_tasks: 1) ENG-2010: add GC sweep for dead operator caches after 14 days inactivity; 2) SEC-849: add attestation proof for immutable-audit-stamp; 3) OPER-340: automate feature flag gradual ramp in console.
